title: Ember and Thorn
premise: Jude Amberdale can speak to beasts—a gift the crown of Vaelmoor has outlawed on pain of death. When a royal decree launches a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted, Jude flees the city of Thornhollow with a ragtag found family: a disgraced knight, a runaway noble's son, and a one-eyed wolf who is more than he seems. She learns the king himself was replaced years ago by a hollow thing called the Regent, sustained by stolen magic harvested from captured gift-bearers—including, she discovers, her own missing mother. To save the kingdom and the people she loves, Jude must infiltrate the palace, unbind the true king from his enchanted sleep beneath the throne, and face the Regent in a battle where her forbidden voice becomes the kingdom's only weapon.
about_author: Isandro Winterbourne is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about outsiders, wild places, and the families we choose when blood fails us.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the market city of Thornhollow, Jude sells harmless charms while secretly bargaining with rats and pigeons for gossip and coin. A near-discovery by a gray-cloaked inquisitor forces her to burn her most dangerous trinket. Beat: the exhausting vigilance of hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: What the Rats Knew
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The city rats warn her that soldiers are mapping every household, hunting something they call 'the gifted.' Her friend Bram, a disgraced knight turned dockworker, urges caution; her ward Pip, a runaway noble's son, begs her to run. Beat: dread arriving ahead of the danger.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The crown announces the Great Hunt: all gift-bearers to be registered, then taken. That night, an old hedge-witch who once sheltered Jude is dragged from her home. Jude watches from a rooftop, unable to intervene. Beat: guilt as the price of survival.

chapters.title: One-Eye
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A scarred wolf appears at her door, speaking in a voice like gravel and old grief. He claims he knew her mother, who vanished three years ago after 'going to the palace.' He offers to lead Jude out of the city. Beat: the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: Burning Thornhollow Bridge
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Inquisitors raid the tenements. Bram covers their escape and is captured buying time. Jude, Pip, and One-Eye flee across the marshes as the city gates close behind them. Beat: rage and helplessness, the family broken open.

chapters.title: The Marsh Road
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The fugitives navigate the drowned country, and Pip reveals he ran from a father who sold his sister to the Hunt. Jude teaches him small beast-speech tricks for foraging and warning. Beat: tentative trust forming between two damaged people.

chapters.title: The Hollow Village
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They find a village where every gift-bearer has already been taken, leaving only silence—no dogs bark, no birds sing. An old man tells them the taken are carted north 'to feed the crown.' Beat: horror made quiet and ordinary.

chapters.title: Wolves at the Ford
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Inquisitor hounds corner them at a river crossing. Jude speaks to the pack leader and turns the hunt back on its handlers, revealing her power to Pip fully for the first time. Beat: terror transformed into awe—and fear of what she's becoming.

chapters.title: The Wolf's Memory
chapters.summary: One-Eye's POV (rendered through Jude hearing him). The wolf shares his memory: Jude's mother entering the palace willingly, trading herself to protect her daughter's name from the registers. Beat: inheritance reframed—not just a gift, but a debt.

chapters.title: Sanctum Beneath the Hill
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. They reach a hidden sanctuary of surviving gift-bearers led by Maren, a blind seer who recognizes Jude's voice as 'the deep kind'—able to speak not just to beasts but to enchantments themselves. Beat: belonging offered, and feared.

chapters.title: Lessons in Deep Speech
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Jude trains with Maren, learning to hear the magic woven into objects and wards. Her first attempt to unbind a simple charm nearly kills her—the deep speech takes something from the speaker each time. Beat: power with a cost.

chapters.title: The Seer's Price
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Maren reveals the truth: the king sleeps beneath the throne, bound by the Regent, a construct fed on harvested gifts. Only deep speech can unbind him—but the last person who tried was Jude's mother, and she did not fail. She was kept. Beat: the quest becomes personal.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. A sanctuary member, terrified for his own children, sells their location to the Hunt. The sanctuary burns. Maren stays behind to hold the wards and dies buying the others time. Beat: betrayal, sacrifice, and the collapse of safe harbor.

chapters.title: Ashes and Arguments
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The survivors fracture—some want to hide forever, others to fight. Jude, grieving Maren, chooses the impossible: go to the capital, enter the palace, wake the king. Pip refuses to let her go alone. Beat: resolve forged in loss.

chapters.title: The Capital of Bells
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The group infiltrates Aurelmark using Pip's forgotten noble name and his sister's fate as cover. They witness a public 'registration' that is really a harvesting, and see the Regent in person for the first time—beautiful, wrong, smiling. Beat: the enemy given a face.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Posing as a captured gift-bearer, Jude lets herself be taken into the palace depths. In the harvesting cells she finds her mother—alive, hollowed, barely recognizable. Beat: reunion as heartbreak; the mother saved in body but not yet in spirit.

chapters.title: The Voice Beneath the Throne
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Guided by One-Eye through servant tunnels, Jude reaches the vault beneath the throne room and finds the sleeping king, bound in chains of woven song. She begins the unbinding, paying pieces of her own memories as the toll. Beat: sacrifice begun, identity eroding.

chapters.title: The Regent's Offer
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The Regent confronts Jude mid-ritual, offering her mother's restoration and Pip's safety if she stops. It shows her visions of a kingdom at peace under its rule. Pip arrives and shatters the illusion by refusing to be bargained for. Beat: temptation answered with loyalty.

chapters.title: Ember and Thorn
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Climax. The unbinding completes as the king wakes—but the Regent unleashes the harvested magic of hundreds of stolen voices against them. Jude answers with the deep speech, calling every creature in the capital to rise. Beat: the forbidden gift becomes salvation.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The awakened king joins the fight, and together they unravel the Regent thread by thread. Jude pours her final memories into the unmaking—forgetting her mother's face even as her mother wakes beside her. Beat: victory purchased with selfhood.

chapters.title: What Remains of Jude Amberdale
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Aftermath. The king abolishes the Hunt; the gifted are freed. Jude remembers everything except her childhood, and must meet her mother as a stranger. Pip, Bram (freed from the cells), and One-Eye surround her. Beat: grief and grace intertwined.

chapters.title: A Family, Chosen
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Epilogue. On the rebuilt sanctuary hill, Jude teaches the first class of openly gifted children, her mother slowly relearning her daughter's name. Pip calls the group family; no one argues. Beat: inheritance transformed into legacy; identity rebuilt by those who choose you.
